IdempotencyKey.description: Optional, at most 255 characters of valid UTF-8. The only thing that deduplicates a create: a replay with the identical body returns the original object (status 200), a replay with a different body is refused 409. No key means every attempt is its own object.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

Internal.description: `internal` — something went wrong on our side.

NotFound.description: `not_found` — no such object in this key's mode. A live key cannot see test objects nor a test key live ones.

SubscriptionConflict.description: `already_canceled` or `invalid_state` — the request was well formed and would have been legal a moment ago. A retried cancel lands here, which is why it is not a 422.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized` — missing/malformed Authorization header or an invalid/revoked API key.

Unprocessable.description: `invalid_request` — the body is malformed or a field is unusable. `error.message` names what to fix.

Address.description: The buyer's address. Only the PayLater lenders `kredivo` and `indodana` require it; all three parts or it counts as absent.

amount.description: Whole rupiah. Omitted means the whole remaining gross.
Whole rupiah. Authoritative even when order_items is sent.

checkout.description: Everything that shapes the Kasera Pay Checkout page. Sending it, even as `{}`, is what makes this a Checkout create: the buyer walks `checkout_url` and the page collects whatever a chosen method still needs. Omitting it makes the create Direct API: `checkout_url` is still returned, but no page is assumed, so a method that needs a buyer field you did not send is refused 422 `customer_required`, and the three `is_*_required` asks are inherited from the account's payment-method settings. Sending the object replaces all three at once, so an object carrying only `steps` turns those account defaults off for this payment.

customer.description: Who is paying — what payment rails are fulfilled with (not `payer`, which is display data). Methods may require `customer.name` etc.; read `required_customer_fields` on GET /v1/payment_methods.

external_id.description: Your order id. A label — stored, echoed, filterable, never deduplicating.

merchant_ref.description: Your own reference. A label, like external_id.

order_items.description: Display-only detail. Σ price×quantity must equal amount or the create is refused 422 `order_items_mismatch`.

payment_methods.description: Method codes this payment may be paid with, in the order a buyer should be offered them. Omitted or empty means every method enabled on the account. An unknown or disabled code is refused 422 `payment_method_unavailable`, never dropped.

return_url.description: Where the hosted checkout sends the buyer afterwards. https only on live creates; a test key also accepts http, so a store on localhost can develop the full redirect flow.

fields.description: Offending fields as dotted JSON paths of the body you sent (`customer.email`, `order_items.3.price`) mapped to the rule that failed or the offending value.

request_id.description: Echoes the X-Request-Id response header so you can quote the exact failed request to support.

Instructions.description: How-to for the buyer, in Indonesian. Print it verbatim.

percent_bps.description: Percent of gross in basis points.

min_amount.description: Smallest amount a create on this method accepts, in whole rupiah, for this account. Each method has its own range.

required_customer_fields.description: `customer.*` paths a create naming this method must send. Always an array, `[]` when the method needs nothing.

type.description: The `payment.type` this method's payload will carry.

PaymentPayload.description: The method-shaped payload, a discriminated union keyed on `type`. Omitted entirely until the rail has issued something for the buyer to use — never a placeholder. Only the fields belonging to the live `type` are populated.

display_name.description: Long label, e.g. `Mandiri Virtual Account` or `Credit Card`.

payment_code.description: The Virtual Account number the buyer types into their banking app (`type: payment_code`).

qr_string.description: Raw EMV QRIS payload (`type: qr`) — encode it into a QR client-side.

redirect_url.description: Where to send the buyer (`type: redirect`). Present only while pending.

phone.description: payer.phone must be E.164; customer.phone also accepts the local Indonesian format (e.g. `08123456789`).

failure_reason.description: The processor's own words when status is failed.

status.description: `pending` is a refund the processor never answered; it holds its amount until a human resolves it.

Subscription.description: `status` and `paid_through` answer different questions and both matter. `status` is where the subscription sits in its lifecycle; `paid_through` is whether the customer may use the service right now. Grant access on `paid_through`: an integration that reads `status` alone cuts off every `past_due` subscriber inside the grace period they have already paid for.

current_period_end.description: When the next invoice is raised.

ends_at.description: A cancellation already scheduled for the period end.

is_test.description: Which mode this subscription belongs to. Always present, `false` included — a missing field would have to be read as live.

paid_through.description: Service access lapses at this instant. Absent until something has been paid for.

pending_plan_id.description: A change waiting for the next renewal. This is what the next invoice will use.

test_clock.description: Where this sandbox subscription's clock stands, when it has been advanced. Absent on live subscriptions, which have no clock to move.

SubscriptionInvoice.description: One billing cycle's bill. It carries what the customer owes and nothing about Kasera's fee — that is on the transaction named by `payment_request_id`, which you can fetch from `GET /v1/transactions/{id}`.

amount_due.description: Still owed. This is the figure to show a payer.

due_at.description: When payment is expected. Not the payment attempt's expiry — a QRIS code lives an hour and the invoice link outlives it.

paid_externally.description: Recorded by the merchant rather than collected by Kasera. Settled, but not Kasera-processed volume — keep the two apart in reporting.

payment_request_id.description: `payreq_<uuid>` — the live collection attempt, absent when there is none.

status.description: `void` withdraws the debt; `uncollectible` admits it is still owed and no longer being chased.

archived.description: A superseded version. Still readable; no new subscription may start on it.

version.description: Which version of `code` this is. An invoice records the version it was billed on, so a repriced plan never restates an old bill.

amount.description: Gross, whole rupiah. `amount = fee + net`, always.

checkout_url.description: The hosted Kasera Pay Checkout page for this payment.

livemode.description: false on objects a test key created — no real money moves.

payment_method.description: Lowercase code of the method this payment was created for — read off the row, not today's catalogue.

source.description: Which channel created this request. Always `api` here; history read back may also say `merchant`, `payment_page` or `unknown`.

has_more.description: More rows behind this page — pass the last id as starting_after.

WebhookEvent.description: The `payment.paid` delivery POSTed to your webhook endpoint. Verify `Kasera-Signature-V1` (`t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`; each `v1` is lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over `<unix>.<raw body>` with your endpoint's signing secret; reject if `t` is older than five minutes; accept if any `v1` matches, since two are sent during a secret-rotation grace). The legacy body-only `Kasera-Signature` header is still sent but deprecated. Dedupe on `id` (also sent as the `Kasera-Event-Id` header). Delivery is at-least-once.

WebhookTestPing.description: The dashboard's test delivery — proof that signing and connectivity work, carrying nothing that looks like money. Signed and headed exactly like a real event.

apiKey.description: An API key from the dashboard's Developer page: `kp_live_...` or `kp_test_...`.

info.description:
The public developer API. Create payment requests, read them back, list
the payment methods your account may offer, and refund card payments.

All amounts are whole rupiah (no decimals): `amount = fee + net`, always.
Timestamps are ISO-8601 with a `+07:00` offset. Ids are self-describing:
`payreq_<uuid>` for transactions, `rfd_<uuid>` for refunds.

## Authentication

Every endpoint (except this document) requires a bearer API key in the
`Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer kp_live_...` or
`Bearer kp_test_...`. A test key sees and creates only test objects, a
live key only live ones — the other mode's objects answer 404. Requests
are limited to 300 per minute per key; failed authentication is throttled
per IP.

## Idempotency

`POST /v1/transactions` and `POST /v1/refunds` accept an optional
`Idempotency-Key` header — the ONLY thing that deduplicates a create.
Replaying a key with the identical body returns the original object with
status 200 (not 201); replaying it with a different body is refused
409 `idempotency_conflict`. `merchant_ref` and `external_id` are labels:
stored, echoed, filterable, never deduplicating.

## Pagination

Lists return `{data, has_more}` pages ordered newest first. Pass
`starting_after` with the last `id` you saw to fetch the next page;
`limit` is 1–100, default 20.

## Webhooks

Kasera Pay POSTs a `payment.paid` event to your configured endpoint when
a payment settles, carrying `Kasera-Event-Id` for deduplication and two
signature headers:

- `Kasera-Signature-V1` — verify this one. Format `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`,
  where each `v1` is lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over `<unix>.<raw body>`
  keyed with your endpoint's signing secret. Reject deliveries whose `t`
  is older than five minutes. During the 24 hours after a secret
  rotation the header carries two `v1` entries, one per secret; accept
  the delivery if any entry matches.
- `Kasera-Signature` — deprecated. Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
  body alone, with no timestamp, so a captured delivery replays forever.
  Still sent for existing verifiers; it will be removed after a
  deprecation period announced on the webhook docs page. New
  integrations must not rely on it.

Delivery is at-least-once with backoff over ~34 hours. The payload
shapes are `WebhookEvent` and `WebhookTestPing` under components/schemas.
info.title: Kasera Pay API

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.0 document describing this API.

get.description: The method codes a create may name in `payment_methods`, with each method's fee, amount bounds and required `customer.*` fields. Read this instead of hard-coding codes — methods can be enabled or suspended without a release on your side.

post.description: Returns money on a succeeded card payment, in full (omit `amount`) or in part. QRIS and Virtual Account refunds are manual. The same optional `Idempotency-Key` contract as creating a transaction — a replayed key returns the original refund and never reaches the card processor again.

201.description: The refund as it stands once the processor answered.

502.description: `refund_refused` — nothing was refunded, safe to retry — or `refund_unresolved` — the amount is held pending and must NOT be retried; contact support.

get.description: Closed beta. Every subscription endpoint answers 404 for accounts we have not enabled by hand, and the shape may change before general availability.

post.description: Sending an `external_id` you have used before updates that customer instead of creating a second one, which is what makes re-running an import safe. One of `email` or `phone` is required: a customer nobody can be reached at cannot be sent a renewal reminder.

email_opted_out.description: They asked not to be emailed. Email is opt-out where WhatsApp is opt-in.

external_id.description: Your own identifier. Matching on it is what makes a re-import an update.

whatsapp_opted_in.description: They agreed to be messaged on WhatsApp. Without it no WhatsApp reminder is ever scheduled for them.

patch.description: Edits the customer at this id and never creates one. Use this rather than the create endpoint when correcting an `external_id`: that one matches on `external_id`, so changing it there mints a second customer and leaves the subscriptions pointing at the first. Every field is replaced by what you send, and the same rule as creating applies — one of `email` or `phone` must survive the edit.

external_id.description: Unique among your customers. 422 if another of yours already holds it.

200.description: The customer as it now stands.

get.description: Only the current version of each plan. Archived versions stay readable through the subscriptions that reference them.

200.description: The plans a new subscription may start on.

post.description:
Plans are immutable. Posting a `code` you have used before writes the next version and archives the one it replaces — subscribers stay on the version they signed up to until you move them, and their existing invoices keep the price they were issued at.

`amount` is required even when it is 0: a free plan is a real plan, so an absent field cannot be read as a free one.

Daily, weekly, monthly and annual. Anything longer than a year is refused.

amount.description: Whole rupiah per cycle. 0 is a free plan.

code.description: Stable across versions; what ties a plan's history together.

discount_amount.description: A flat reduction per cycle. Cannot exceed `amount`.

setup_amount.description: Charged once, on the first invoice only.

trial_days.description: A trial raises no invoice at all. Access runs to the trial's end and the first bill is issued when it expires.

post.summary: [Beta] Create a plan, or reprice one

post.description:
Bills the opening cycle immediately and returns with the first invoice already issued — unless the plan has a trial, which raises nothing until it ends.

The mode follows your key: a `kp_test_` key creates a sandbox subscription, which raises sandbox payment requests and sends no reminders to anybody.

Live subscriptions are for verified accounts only: until verification is through, a live key is answered `403 verification_required` and nothing is written. A sandbox key works throughout.

start_at.description: RFC3339. The day the first cycle opens, and the calendar day every later cycle anchors to. Defaults to today.

403.description: `verification_required` — live subscriptions need a verified account; use a sandbox key meanwhile.

post.description:
Simulate the passage of time so a renewal can be watched without waiting for one.

This bills nothing itself. It moves the subscription's own clock; the renewal sweep then does on its next pass exactly what it does in production — issues the invoice for each cycle passed, creates the QRIS request, and extends access when it is paid. A simulation running its own billing path would be testing code nobody runs.

Advances accumulate, so a year of renewals can be walked one call at a time. It only moves forward: rewinding would put a subscription behind cycles it has already billed.

Sandbox only. A live subscription is refused `422`.

to.description: RFC3339. Where the subscription's clock should stand after this call — later than where it stands now, which the `test_clock` field reports.

200.description: The subscription, with its clock moved.

post.summary: [Beta, test mode] Move a sandbox subscription's clock forward

post.description:
`at_period_end: false` (the default) stops access immediately. `at_period_end: true` honours the service already paid for and stops when the current period runs out. Neither refunds anything.

Cancellation is final. A payment arriving afterwards settles its invoice — the debt was real — and grants no access and restarts no billing. Cancelling an already-cancelled subscription is `409`.

Takes effect at the next renewal, and only then. There is no immediate option: proration is not available in this release, and applying a paid upgrade before it is paid for would grant service nobody authorised.

The scheduled values appear as `pending_plan_id` and `pending_quantity` until the renewal applies them.

200.description: The subscription, with the change pending.

post.summary: [Beta] Schedule a plan or quantity change

post.description: Stops billing, and stops access with it. A pause is not a free month.
Returns to `active`, or to `past_due` when an invoice is still outstanding — the pause did not settle the debt.

get.description: One page of this key's payment requests, newest first, scoped to the key's mode. Malformed filters are refused 422, never silently dropped.

parameters.description: Page size, 1–100. Out of range falls back to 20.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The last `id` of the previous page (`payreq_<uuid>`). A cursor that does not name one of your payment requests is refused 422 `invalid_cursor`.
parameters.name: starting_after

post.description:
Creates a payment request and, for headless integrations, attaches the
rail's payload (`payment`) when it can be generated immediately. Send
the buyer to `checkout_url`, or render `payment` in your own screens.
A replayed `Idempotency-Key` with the identical body returns the
original with status 200.

200.description: Idempotent replay — the original payment request.

400.description: `invalid_idempotency_key` — the header is over 255 characters or not valid UTF-8.

409.description: `idempotency_conflict` — this Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.

422.description: `validation_failed`, `invalid_body`, `order_items_mismatch`, `payment_method_unavailable`, `customer_required`, `amount_too_small`, `amount_too_large`, `expiry_too_long` or `expiry_too_short` — `error.fields` names the offending fields as dotted JSON paths.
